newsitem.title: USA: Rite Aid unit tenders for Thrifty 2004 debt.
newsitem.headline: Rite Aid unit tenders for Thrifty 2004 debt.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp on Monday announced it has set a tender offer and consent solicitation through unit Rite Investments Corp for the 12-1/4 percent senior subordinated notes of Thrifty Payless Inc.

Rite Aid completed a merger with Thrifty Payless in a deal valued at $1.4 billion on December 12. The merger created a chain of more than 3,500 drugstores with annual revenues of more than $10 billion.

The purchase price for the notes will be 35 basis points over the yield of the seven percent U.S. Treasury Note due April 15, 1999, on Jan. 16, 1997, less a consent payment of $5 per $1,000 in note principal, Rite Aid said.
If the offer is extended, the price will be set on the third business day prior to the expiration date.

Rite Aid is also soliciting consents to eliminate substantially all of the restrictive covenants and certain default provisions in the indenture. The consent does not apply to the covenants to pay interest and principal of the notes and the related default provisions, Rite Aid said.
The offer is conditioned on consent from holders of at least two-thirds of the notes.

The consent payment will be paid to holders who tender their notes and give consent at or prior to midnight, EST, on one business day following an announcement that the requisite consents were received or on January 13, 1997.
The offer will expire on January 22, 1997, provided there is a minimum of five business days between the consent date and the expiration of the offer.
NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc is the dealer manager for the offer and consent solicitation.
